title: Addition and condensation polymers
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point covers the whole brief: chem-addition-polymers teaches only addition polymers with nothing lost, and chem-condensation-polymers teaches only condensation polymers with a small molecule lost, so no single point matches the new point as written.

draft.title: Addition and condensation polymers
card: Monomers with a carbon-carbon double bond join by opening that bond. Every atom in the monomers ends up in the polymer, so nothing is lost.
Monomers join by reacting at functional groups on their ends. Each time two monomers link, a small molecule such as water is released.
A condensation monomer needs a reactive group at each end, such as an acid group or an alcohol group. This lets the chain keep growing in both directions.
To classify a polymer, ask whether a small molecule is given off when it forms. If none is, it is an addition polymer. If one is, it is a condensation polymer.
draft.remember: Addition: nothing lost. Condensation: a small molecule such as water is released.

a.q: Which observation shows that a polymer forms by condensation polymerisation?
opts: Water is released each time two monomers link
The monomers each contain a C=C double bond
The polymer has a larger mass than one monomer
The polymer forms as a very long carbon chain
a.why: A small molecule such as water is given off at each link, so atoms are lost from the monomers. A polymer is always heavier than one monomer, so that does not tell the types apart.
a.clue: Think about what leaves the reaction.

b.q: In a lab, 100 g of a monomer is fully converted to polymer. The polymer has a mass of 100 g and no other product forms. What type of polymerisation is it?
opts: Addition, because no atoms were lost from the monomer
Condensation, because the monomer joined into chains
Addition, because the monomer must contain an acid group
Condensation, because the polymer has a very large mass
b.why: The polymer has the same mass as the monomer used, so no small molecule was released. That fits addition polymerisation. Forming long chains happens in both types, so it does not suggest condensation.
b.clue: Compare the mass before and after.

a.best: Water is released each time two monomers link

b.best: Addition, because no atoms were lost from the monomer
